lines.text: Unit 02 Spread of Islam
DevelopmentofIslamicArtandCulture
The Umayad period is considered to be a critical period in the development of islamic art
and culture. The Umayads gave great importance to.education and opened many houses
of scholars, bookstores and schools.
Architecture
Art of that era was influenced by multiple sources. These include Coptic tradition of
present-day Egypt and Syria, Sassanian metalwork and crafts from what is now Iraq, and
Byzantine mosaics depicting animals and plants. Despite all this, Muslim architects
produced original works based on their beliefs. The Umayyads are considered to be
pioneers in IslamicArt.Tradition of adding minarets and mihrabto the Masajid began with
the Umayyads.
Abeautiful example of suchwork is DomeoftheRock (Kubbat al-Sahra) inJerusalem.It
was one of the first Islamic buildings ever constructed. It was built between 685 and 692
by Abd al-Malik. The mosaics in the Dome of the Rock contain no human figures or
animals. You can see its picture on the first page of this chapter.
Another piece of early Islamic art that survived till today is Umayyad Mosque in
Damascus.Its constructionwas started byWalid-l in706ADwhichwas finished in715AD
during the reign of Suleman bin Abdul Malik.

Language and Literature
